sections.title: Objective type questions: each has four statements or pairs of ½ mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or arrange in sequence).

questions.q: Match the right with the example: (i) Right to safety (ii) Right to choose (iii) Right to be informed (iv) Right to seek redressal; (a) a shopkeeper keeps only one brand of toothpaste (b) a cooker bursts (c) a shopkeeper refuses to give the product booklet (d) compensation for faulty goods.
Match the standard mark with the product: (i) ISI (ii) FPO (iii) Agmark (iv) Hallmark; (a) gold ornaments (b) jams and pickles (c) spices and pulses (d) pressure cookers.

State True or False: (i) A shopkeeper can charge more than MRP for a product in a cinema hall. (ii) MRP includes all taxes. (iii) Imitating logos and packaging is a criminal offence. (iv) A label should show the lot or batch number.

Fill in the blanks: (i) A person who buys goods or services is a ______. (ii) The element added to a food stuff to lower its quality is an ______. (iii) Selling goods at higher prices during shortage is ______ marketing. (iv) World Consumer Rights Day is observed on ______ March.
Match the food with its adulterant: (i) Milk (ii) Black pepper (iii) Tea leaves (iv) Tea or semolina; (a) papaya seeds (b) water (c) iron filings (d) coloured exhausted leaves.

Match the forum with the value of goods: (i) District (ii) State (iii) National (iv) Lok Adalat; (a) above Rs 1 crore (b) up to Rs 20 lakh (c) Rs 20 lakh to Rs 1 crore (d) not a consumer forum for this case.

State True or False: (i) Buy non-perishables in bulk. (ii) Buy perishables in large quantities. (iii) Take the bill even if you pay a little extra. (iv) Buy electronics and woollens in the off season.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) False – in small quantities. (iii) True. (iv) True.

questions.q: Which of these show defective measures or weights? (i) False-bottomed milk measure (ii) Magnet under the balance pan (iii) Stamp of an inspector with date (iv) Stones used instead of weights.
questions.answer: (i), (ii) and (iv) show defective measures; (iii) is a sign of a proper measure.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: In what four ways do consumer organisations help the consumers?
questions.answer: They give information; test products for quality and defects; educate consumers; protest against anti-consumer activities; guide the government in framing policies; accept complaints and represent consumers in consumer courts.

or.q: Write any four responsibilities of a consumer.
or.answer: Survey the market before buying; insist on and keep the bill; buy standard-mark products; read and follow instructions; buy sealed foods; file a complaint in the proper forum and join other consumers against sellers; do not encourage black marketing.

questions.q: What is the importance of the information given on the label of a product?
questions.answer: It gives the name, ingredients (allergies or animal source), manufacturer's address, directions and warnings, net weight, MRP, batch number for complaints, and the dates of manufacture and expiry, the standard mark and guarantee, so we can choose, use safely and complain if needed.

or.q: Why is it important to check the standard mark, ingredients, batch number and expiry date on the label?
or.answer: Standard mark shows quality, ingredients show allergens, batch number is needed to complain to the manufacturer, and expiry date tells us not to buy products near expiry.

questions.q: Mr Gupta wants to file a case against a manufacturer. What two documents would he need to submit with his complaint?
questions.answer: The bill or receipt (proof of purchase) and the guarantee/warranty or a notarised affidavit with the prescribed form (plus the court fee).

questions.q: Adulteration is a major problem of consumers. Support this statement with any four examples.
questions.answer: Water is added to milk; papaya seeds to black pepper; resin or gum to asafoetida; coloured exhausted leaves to tea; dung powder to coriander powder; iron filings to tea or semolina; extraneous colour to spices.

questions.q: Which adulterants are added to asafoetida, spices, milk and black pepper and how are they tested?
questions.answer: Asafoetida – resin or gum; shake in water – pure hing turns milky. Spices – extraneous colour; sprinkle in water – coloured water. Milk – water; a drop on a tilted plate leaves no trace. Black pepper – papaya seeds; in water pepper settles and papaya seeds float.

questions.q: Elaborate six points of information you would check on the label of honey before buying.
questions.answer: Name of the product and brand; manufacturer's name and address; ingredients; net weight; MRP; dates of manufacture and expiry or best before; batch number; standard mark such as Agmark or FPO.

questions.q: How can you check whether the milk vendor is cheating you?
questions.answer: Check that milk is measured to the brim, the measure is emptied completely before refilling, there is no false bottom, and the measure has the inspector's stamp with date; test dilution with a tilted plate or by keeping it in a tumbler.

questions.q: How can the cloth merchant cheat in measuring? Name any four signs.
questions.answer: Using a table to measure, a bent measuring rod, stretching the fabric while measuring, and selling cheap fabric at the price of a better one.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Write any six characteristic features of a good label of a food product.
questions.answer: Name of the product and brand; manufacturer's name and address; ingredients; date of manufacture and date of expiry; net weight; MRP; directions for use and storage; standard mark (Agmark, FPO, ISI); lot or batch number; guarantee or warnings.

questions.q: Explain any six problems faced by a consumer and how to tackle one of them.
questions.answer: Price variation (charging above MRP); lack of standardised products; imitation of brands and marks; adulteration; hoarding and black marketing; defective weights and measures; misleading advertisements and sales; poor services. To tackle price variation: survey the market, never pay more than MRP and take a bill to complain.

questions.q: Describe the steps of filing a complaint in a consumer court.
questions.answer: Contact the seller and keep a record; write to the manufacturer by registered post; send a notice to the opposite party giving 15 days; fill the prescribed form with details and facts, attach bills and court fee, specify compensation and attach a notarised affidavit; submit to the receiving clerk of the consumer court (district up to Rs 20 lakh, state up to Rs 1 crore, national above that); the court notifies the other party who must reply in 30 days; the case is to be settled in 90 days.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain any five rights of a consumer with an example of each.
questions.answer: (1) Right to safety – a cooker that bursts or adulterated food; complain against the manufacturer. (2) Right to choose – a shopkeeper cannot keep just one brand of toothpaste. (3) Right to be informed – a shopkeeper who refuses the product booklet can be taken to court. (4) Right to be heard – express yourself in court if cheated. (5) Right to seek redressal – compensation for faulty goods or unfair trade practices. (6) Right to consumer education – knowledge of consumer evils. (7) Right to basic needs and a healthy environment.

questions.q: Write the consumer aids available to a consumer and the information a label must give (five points each).
questions.answer: Aids: labels, leaflets, packages, advertisements, standardisation marks (ISI, FPO, Agmark, Woolmark, Hallmark, Eco-mark), legislation (Consumer Protection Act) and consumer organisations. A label gives the name of the product, manufacturer's name and address, ingredients, directions for use, warnings, date of manufacture and expiry, net weight, MRP, batch number, guarantee period and the standard mark.
